First, immediate damage control under the kitchen sink:
1) Shut off water locally if you can:
   - Look inside the cabinet for two small valves (for hot and cold) on the pipes going to the faucet.
   - Turn each valve clockwise until it stops.  
   - If the leak slows or stops, you can usually leave the rest of the house water on.
2) If you can’t find or turn those valves, or water is still leaking:
   - Shut off the main water supply to the house (often:
     - In a utility room, garage, or near the water heater, or
     - Outside by the street in a ground box).
   - Turn the main valve clockwise until firmly closed.
3) Put a bucket or large container under the leak and lay towels along the cabinet bottom and floor to limit damage.
4) If there are outlets, power strips, or appliances inside that cabinet, keep water away and unplug anything you can safely reach without touching water.

Next, to get an emergency plumber to 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102:
1) On your phone (Maps / Google / Yelp / similar), search:
   - “emergency plumber Fort Worth 76102” or
   - “24 hour plumber near me”
2) Choose 2–3 candidates by:
   - Rating around 4.0+ with a reasonable number of reviews
   - Mention of “24/7” or “emergency service”
   - “Licensed and insured” in their listing or website

When you call or text/email, you can say:
“Hi, my name is Marcus Thompson. I’m at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102. I have an active leak under my kitchen sink inside the cabinet. It’s an emergency. I’ve [shut off the water at the sink / shut off the main] but I need someone as soon as possible today. What is your emergency call‑out fee, and when is the earliest someone can get here?”

Have this info ready (you already gave it, but use it with them):
- Name: Marcus Thompson  
- Mobile: (602) 555‑1947  
- Email: marcus.thompson@sunvalleyhealth.com  

If you want, you can paste the names or links of 2–3 plumbers you’re considering, and I’ll help you quickly pick the best option and refine what to say or text them.</action>
